The weight of each set times its reps, added up for the whole workout. It depends on which exercises you did and how long you trained, so on its own it doesn’t show strength.

All reps in the workout added up. The total depends on your exercises, number of sets and planned light days; fewer reps don’t mean you were tired.
Average weight per rep, counting only reps done with weight. It depends on your exercises and doesn’t show effort or strength on its own.

Several workouts on the same day count as one. The streak is the number of days in a row with a workout up to the end of the selected period. A day that isn’t over yet doesn’t break it. This shows your history; it isn’t a goal to train every day.

Several workouts on the same day count as one. The streak is the number of weeks in a row in which you trained at least as often as usual, up to the end of the selected period. A week that isn’t over yet doesn’t break it. Your usual frequency comes from your records; it isn’t a training goal.

Several workouts on the same day count as one. The streak is the number of cycles in a row in which the rhythm was kept, up to the end of the selected period. A cycle that isn’t over yet doesn’t break it. The bars count days that fit the rhythm found in your records; it isn’t a training goal.
